text.p: Northeast Utilities said Friday it was investigating a recent temperature rise in the spent fuel pool of its Millstone 3 nuclear power plant, even though the situation has since been corrected.
"While the technical consequences of this event were minor, we are taking this situation very seriously," said Buzz Carns, Millstone's chief nuclear operator.
The company is conducting technical and independent reviews, to find out what happened and why, Carns said.

Northeast's three Millstone units have been closed for safety reasons since March of 1996. The utility has said it expects to have Millstone 3 ready for restart by the end of September, pending approval by federal regulators.
Analysts have said that the eventual restart of the Millstone plants will be crucial to Northeast's financial survival.
Northeast has projected its nuclear-related losses at $990 million through 1998.
Connecticut regulators said Friday that Northeast may not ask ratepayers to help cover losses at the Millstone plants.
Northeast said it will appeal the ruling by the Connecticut Department of Public Utility Control.
Northeast said it notified the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and state authorities of the Millstone 3 temperature rise even though it was not required to do so.
Initial analysis suggests that the event was caused by an incomplete changeover from one cooling system to another, Northeast said.
The changeover occurred early Wednesday morning, and was detected on Thursday morning.

The pool, which had been at 87 degrees Fahrenheit, rose to about 97 degrees. Northeast said the pool's design limit temperature is 140 degrees, and an alarm would sound in the control room if the temperature reached 135 degrees.
